answer: A ski pass with lift-gate scan history proves a body was on a mountain: the resort sells one pass per person, photographs the holder, and logs every gate scan. An orchard of fake accounts with no scans is worthless, and a wharf of passes bought in bulk still needs one photographed face per pass plus the lift ticket price. The karst of cheap identities evaporates because each pass costs $800 a season and the scans must show plausible, spaced-out days on the slopes. Reusing one face across many passes trips the photo match, so every identity needs a new face and a new pass.
